title: Dispersive dielectric slab in WR-90: ε∞ = 2 with a Debye and a Lorentz pole, 20 mm
source: TE10 transmission-line cascade with the complex propagation constant β = √(k0² ε(ω) − (π/a)²) in the slab (D. M. Pozar, Microwave Engineering, 4th ed., Wiley 2012, §3.3 and §4.4), ε(ω) = ε∞ + Δε_D/(1 + jωτ) + Δε_L ω0²/(ω0² − ω² + jωγ) for e^{jωt} (A. Taflove, S. C. Hagness, Computational Electrodynamics, 3rd ed., Artech House 2005, §9.2 and §9.4), both evaluated by ABCD matrices separately from EMCraft's code

quantities.reason: second-order elements of 3 mm, as for the lossy slab (error about 1e-3 in S, 0.01 dB here where |S21| ≈ 0.6)
the shortest wavelength in the slab (εr′ ≈ 3.3): about ten elements per guide wavelength
the discretisation error of the lossy slab (1.8e-3 at εr = 2.2) at a higher εr′ of 3.0–3.3: a shorter wavelength at the same element size; ε(ω) enters each frequency's mass matrix exactly
